content: Public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants last year, £1.3bn (62%) more than in 2019-20, with spending remaining above pre-pandemic levels. Keir Starmer’s government plans to halve this outlay, but since taking office nearly £650m in new consultancy contracts have been awarded, many set in motion before the handover. KPMG secured a contract worth up to £223m to train civil servants over the next 15 months, its second-largest public sector deal. Labour peer and academic Prem Sikka condemned the dependence on consultants, arguing they add little value and cannot quickly grasp complex organisations. Is there anything else I can help with?
